STEP 1 - Vessel type: flat square plate (white, rim band visible, flat centre, no inner wall).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium-large, around 25 cm wide.
b) Reference: no fork or spoon in full view. The leaves are about 8-10 cm long each, and the plate spans roughly 2.5-3 leaf lengths across, which gives about 24-27 cm.
Reconciled width: 25 cm (area 625 cm2).

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Spinach/leafy greens (raw, mostly wilted spinach with some red-stemmed chard leaves) cover about 20% of the plate, roughly 125 cm2.
- Loose leaves: average thickness about 3 cm at the mound centre (a pile of loose leaves, roughly 3-6 cm, but this is a sparse heap, so take the lower end, about 2 cm average).
- Volume = 125 cm2 x 2 cm = 250 ml.
- Bulk density raw leafy greens = 0.15 g/ml, so mass = 250 x 0.15 = 38 g.
- Add a few small pale stem/white pieces and red chard stalk; these are included in the leaf estimate.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer or hidden food beneath; the greens sit directly on the plate. No extra items.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g: raw spinach/chard about 23 kcal per 100 g.

Total ≈ 38 g, about 9 kcal.
